pdlmi applyPutinar

Documents/pdlmi/applyPutinar
DirectLPólyaL.applyPolya(p)PutinarL.applyPutinar()Full BoxL.applyFullBoxPreorder()

Purpose

Section titled “Purpose”

Create a new pdlmi that represents the stored residual with the implemented cell-local Putinar box Bernstein-Gram certificate.

Syntax

Section titled “Syntax”

Description

Section titled “Description”

The no-argument form selects the smallest admissible absolute order

r={⌊m/2⌋,ℓ=1,⌈m/2⌉,ℓ≥2,r=\begin{cases} \left\lfloor m/2\right\rfloor,&\ell=1,\\ \left\lceil m/2\right\rceil,&\ell\ge2, \end{cases}r={⌊m/2⌋,⌈m/2⌉,​ℓ=1,ℓ≥2,​

where mmm is C.Residual.Degree and ℓ\ellℓ is the parameter count. The explicit form selects order; it does not add order to the residual degree. Both forms rebuild from C.Residual and C.Relation, return a new value object, and leave C unchanged. Applying Putinar after Pólya, full box, or an earlier Putinar order therefore replaces that selection rather than compounding it.

For each physical cell and active rate row, pdlmi first sign-normalizes the target: a >= residual is used directly and a <= residual is negated. In one parameter, the method dispatches to the same parity-specific Markov–Lukács form as applyFullBoxPreorder. For two or more parameters, it represents the target as

S0(α)+∑s=1ℓαs(1−αs)Ss(α).S_0(\boldsymbol\alpha) +\sum_{s=1}^{\ell} \alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)S_s(\boldsymbol\alpha).S0​(α)+s=1∑ℓ​αs​(1−αs​)Ss​(α).

At order rrr, S0S_0S0​ uses a tensor Bernstein Gram basis of degree r1r\mathbf 1r1. The multiplier SsS_sSs​ uses degree r1−esr\mathbf 1-\mathbf e_sr1−es​; a block is omitted if that vector has a negative component. Every present Gram matrix is constrained positive semidefinite. The target is exactly elevated and matched coefficient by coefficient at tensor degree 2r12r\mathbf 12r1.

For an entry-wise inequality, each MATLAB column-major scalar entry receives an independent scalar certificate. Each cell and rate row receives independent dense Gram blocks and independent coefficient equalities. The method does not share Gram variables across cells, insert a positivity margin, call optimize, or choose a solver.

Arguments

Section titled “Arguments”
InputDescription
CAny pdlmi object. Its stored Residual and Relation are the source for the rebuilt certificate.
orderOptional finite nonnegative integer scalar. It is an absolute Gram order and must satisfy r≥⌊m/2⌋r\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloorr≥⌊m/2⌋ in one parameter or r≥⌈m/2⌉r\ge\lceil m/2\rceilr≥⌈m/2⌉ in two or more parameters.

Returned Object

Section titled “Returned Object”

Cputinar is a new pdlmi with UsePolya=false, UseFullBoxPreorder=false, UsePutinar=true, and PutinarOrder equal to the selected order. Within each cell and rate row, Constraints stores the PSD Gram-block conditions before the exact coefficient identities. toYalmip(Cputinar) concatenates those stored entries without changing them.

Deterministic Transcript Example

Section titled “Deterministic Transcript Example”

For the degree-two scalar residual, order one stores two PSD blocks followed by three exact coefficient identities. Order two stores two PSD blocks followed by five identities. Selecting Putinar from polya returns to the stored degree-two residual; it does not use the already elevated constraints.

Validation And Errors

Section titled “Validation And Errors”
  • A malformed order raises pdlmi:InvalidPutinarOrder.
  • A valid integer below ⌊m/2⌋\lfloor m/2\rfloor⌊m/2⌋ in one parameter or ⌈m/2⌉\lceil m/2\rceil⌈m/2⌉ in two or more parameters raises pdlmi:PutinarOrderTooLow.
  • Semidefinite and entry-wise inequalities retain their original global mode.
  • Equality is direct-only; this method raises pdlmi:UnsupportedEqualityCertificate before validating order.
  • Constructor selection errors are documented on the pdlmi constructor page, including pdlmi:InvalidUsePutinar, pdlmi:ConflictingPutinarOptions, and pdlmi:ConflictingRelaxations.

In one parameter, this selector uses the parity-specific Markov–Lukács interval certificate. In two or more parameters it implements only the local-hypercube module generated by the separate factors αs(1−αs)\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)αs​(1−αs​). It is not a general-domain or general-generator Putinar interface, a full-space SOS representation, an automatic order search, or a solver call. Failure at one order does not prove that the target is negative somewhere.

For two or more parameters, the distinct applyFullBoxPreorder method includes every subset product of the same generators. The two selectors share the one-parameter parity rule and default order.
